title: The three parts of a safe while
idea: A safe while loop sets up a value, checks a condition, and updates the value each pass.

exercises.prompt: A safe while loop has three parts. Which three?
options: Set up a starting value, check a condition, update the value each pass
exercises.explanation: Setup before the loop, a condition to test, and an update inside that makes progress. Miss the update and it runs forever.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of a safe while loop to its job.

pairs.right: Give the control value a starting number
Move the value toward the stop each pass

exercises.explanation: Setup starts it, condition tests it, update moves it. All three are needed for a loop that stops.

exercises.prompt:
In this loop, which line is the UPDATE?

i = 0
while i < 4:
    print(i)
    i = i + 1
exercises.explanation: i = i + 1 is the update -- it changes i each pass so the condition will eventually be false.

exercises.prompt:
In the same loop, which line is the SETUP?

i = 0
while i < 4:
    print(i)
    i = i + 1
exercises.explanation: i = 0 is the setup: it gives i a starting value before the loop checks the condition.

exercises.prompt: If a while loop has setup and a condition but no update, it will usually run forever.
exercises.explanation: True. With nothing moving the value, the condition never changes, so the loop can't reach its stop.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the three parts into a working loop that prints 0, 1, 2.
exercises.explanation: Setup (i = 0), condition (while i < 3), body (print i), update (i = i + 1). That order keeps it safe.

exercises.prompt:
This loop is missing its update. Add the line that makes progress:

i = 1
while i <= 3:
    print(i)
    ____
exercises.explanation: Without the update, i stays 1 forever. Adding i = i + 1 lets i reach 4 and stop the loop.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

i = 2
while i < 6:
    print(i)
    i = i + 2
exercises.explanation: i goes 2, 4, then 6. At i = 6 the condition 6 < 6 is false, so it stops. The update adds 2 each pass.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are required for a while loop that stops?
options: A starting value for the control value
A condition that can become false
An update that moves toward the stop
exercises.explanation: Setup, a condition that can turn false, and an update toward it. A print is optional -- not every loop prints.

exercises.prompt: Why is naming the three parts a useful habit?
options: It helps you spot a missing update that would cause an infinite loop
It removes the need to test
exercises.explanation: Checking for setup, condition, AND update catches the most common loop bug before you ever run it.
